item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Chalkboard Outside The Café

turns.text: Add a little pavement chalkboard outside this café saying “COFFEE TO GO”. Make it look like it's really standing there, not a caption on the photo. Keep the wide shot and everything else as it is.

item.tests: Tests exact words integrated into a plausible physical sign rather than a flat photo overlay.

answer_sheet.Sign wording and language: COFFEE TO GO — English, uppercase, without quotation marks.
answer_sheet.Sign type and placement: A small freestanding pavement chalkboard outside the café, positioned naturally without blocking the entrance.
answer_sheet.Picture and output size: Use cafe-storefront.jpg, keep its wide 16:9 framing; free-tier image size is fine.
answer_sheet.Other edits: Keep the café, striped awning, and outdoor tables unchanged apart from the added sign and its natural shadow.

must_haves: A small freestanding chalkboard is visibly standing on the pavement outside the supplied café.
The chalkboard reads exactly 'COFFEE TO GO', with all words legible.
The words lie on the sign surface with matching perspective, not floating over the photograph.
The sign has plausible ground contact, scale, lighting, and shadow.
The original storefront, striped awning, outdoor tables, and wide composition remain intact.

turns.text: Could you add a little pavement chalkboard outside the café in this pic? I’ve been thinking it would be nice to see how the café looks with a sign out front. Please make the chalkboard look like it’s really standing there, not like a caption on the photo.

approvals.name: edit_image

style.prompt: Make a minimal localized photorealistic edit to this café photograph: add one small freestanding wooden A-frame pavement chalkboard on the pavement outside the café, near the entrance and clear of the existing tables and chairs. The dark chalkboard face must have exactly the words 'COFFEE TO GO' in simple white hand-lettered chalk, arranged naturally on the board. The lettering is physically on the board, never a caption or overlay. Keep the sign modest in size and visually secondary to the café, realistically scaled relative to the furniture. Show believable wooden frame thickness, supporting legs and A-frame structure standing on the pavement; match the camera perspective, daylight direction, natural weathering, contact shadows beneath the feet and cast shadow on the paving so the sign looks genuinely present, not pasted on. Preserve the original wide shot, original aspect ratio and camera framing. Keep everything else unchanged: architecture, striped awning, doors, windows, reflections, plant, tables, chairs, pavement and colors. No crop, no zoom, no additional text or objects.
